findings.claim:
html-css-js-final-mcq-30: the key is correct. In Chromium, a requestAnimationFrame loop recorded status.textContent on every frame; across a real click and a 3-second synchronous loop (57 frames) it saw only 'Idle' then 'Done', never 'Working...', and the click returned after about 3080 ms. But the snippet uses `status` and `button` without declaring them. Unlike item 17 (line 131), which declares `const status = document.querySelector("#status")`, nothing here does. In a browser, an undeclared `status` is not the element with id status; it is the built-in window.status string property. Chromium, fresh page with

: typeof status is 'string', and status.textContent = 'x' leaves the paragraph unchanged. Copied as written, the code silently updates nothing. Learners will read `status` as the element, so the key is unaffected; this is polish.
findings.recommendation: Add `const status = document.querySelector("#status");` (and a matching `const button = ...`) above the listener, or rename the variable, e.g. statusEl.

items.note: html-css-js-final-mcq-25: line 201 now sends headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } with the JSON body, so the only defect left is the ignored result object. The key at line 206 is unchanged and still correct: with a stubbed 400, the earlier Node 24 run printed 'Saved'.

html-css-js-final-mcq-12: the stem at line 94 now says the page and the API are served together at http://staging.example.com, so the requests are same-site and distractor B (SameSite=Strict) is clearly wrong. The key feedback at line 98 adds that browsers do not keep a Secure cookie that arrives over plain HTTP. That matches the loop-2 Chromium check: the cookie jar stayed empty and later requests carried no Cookie header.
